tei:elementSpec.tei:desc: A movement instruction. It specifies the position of one controller, e.g. a piano pedal, either as a constant or as a continuous transition towards a target position.

tei:constraintSpec.tei:desc: The positions of the piano pedals (controllers sustain, soft and sostenuto) are normalized to the interval [0.0, 1.0].

schematron:rule.schematron:assert: @="" is out of range. The positions of the piano pedals must be in the interval [0.0, 1.0].

tei:attDef.tei:desc: The movement that this instruction refers to, e.g. one of the piano pedals. All movement elements with the same controller in a movementMap form one continuous curve.

tei:remarks.tei:p: The list is open. Further names can be used to encode other movements of the performer, e.g. the height of a pianist's wrist, a head movement, or the bow position of a string player. The pedal names correspond to the values of MEI's func on pedal.

tei:attDef.tei:desc: The position of the controller at date. For the piano pedals, 0.0 is the rest position (pedal released) and 1.0 the fully depressed pedal; intermediate values express partial depths, e.g. half pedalling.

tei:remarks.tei:p: If omitted, the movement starts where the preceding movement of the same controller ended, i.e. at that movement's transition.to or, if it is constant, at its position. If there is no preceding movement of the same controller, the position is 0.0.
Controllers other than the piano pedals should also use the interval [0.0, 1.0], with 0.0 as the rest position, unless the application defines a different scale.

tei:attDef.tei:desc: If this attribute is specified, the instruction represents a continuous transition from position to the target position given here. The target is reached at the date of the subsequent movement with the same controller. If omitted, the position is constant until then.

If attribute transition.to is specified, the shape of the transition can be further refined by this attribute. Its value in the interval [0.0; 1.0] indicates a distinct sigmoidal (S) shape of the movement (value > 0.0) or a straight linear transition (value = 0.0). The curve is constructed in the same way as that of a continuous dynamics transition.

tei:remarks.tei:p: The default differs from that of dynamics (0.0) because physical movements such as pedal strokes accelerate and decelerate; they are rarely linear.

tei:attDef.tei:desc: If attribute transition.to is specified, the shape of the transition can be further refined by this attribute. Its value in the interval [-1.0; 1.0] indicates whether the movement happens relatively early (value < 0.0), relatively late (value > 0.0) or is equally shared between first and second half of the interval between date and the subsequent movement's date.

tei:exemplum.tei:p: A constant, fully depressed sustain pedal; a quick release of the sustain pedal; a press to half depth that is then held (half pedal); and a slow una corda that is pressed late to 70% of its travel.

tei:remarks.tei:p: The movement instruction starts at the specified date and ends at the date of the subsequent movement instruction with the same controller. Within this time interval the position is either constant, monotonically increasing or monotonically decreasing. Non-monotonic movements (e.g. a pedal that is partly lifted and pressed again) are composed of a sequence of multiple movement elements. A transition should always be followed by another movement instruction of the same controller, as that provides its end date.

MPM encodes the movement, not its acoustic effect. Where, for instance, the dampers of a piano start to lift depends on the instrument. It is up to the rendering engine to map positions to sound, e.g. to MIDI controller 64 (sustain), 67 (soft) or 66 (sostenuto) scaled to the range 0 to 127.
